To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fludarabines and Vidarabinoses are potent inhibitors of human primase and that the mechanism of inhibition is based on a combination of steric and chemical interactions with the enzyme.

the arabinofuranose nucleoside Fludarabin-5′-triphosphate (F-TP) inhibits human primase by binding to its active site, and that this inhibition is mediated by interactions with the catalytic metal ion and with the active site residues Asp 100 and Asp 101.

the structure of Fludara-bine bound to human primase provides a structural basis for the inhibitory activity of arabinose nucleosides towards primase and suggests ways in which the structure of Fluda-bine could be modified in the design of more effective therapeutic agents.
